title: Neuroprotective Effects of Functionalized Hydrophilic Carbon Clusters: Targeted 1 Therapy of Traumatic Brain Injury in an Open Blast Rat Model
content: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) causes multiple cerebrovascular disruptions and oxidative stress, resulting in pathophysiological mechanisms. These are often accompanied by serious impairment in cerebral blood flow autoregulation, as well as neuronal and glial degeneration. Most currently available early antioxidant therapies lack sufficient efficacy. However, the application of a newly developed class of biologically compatible carbon-based nanoclusters, namely poly-ethylene-glycol-functionalized hydrophilic carbon clusters (PEG-HCCs), mitigate secondary injury after a TBI in early studies. In the present pilot study, we explore the efficacy of PEG-HCCs in an open blast rat model of TBI. Here we report on the neuroprotective efficacy of PEG-HCCs.
